title: Derived scalar extension of locally finite free module sheaves
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Work with sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $M$ be an $R$-module sheaf such that every object of the site has a covering on each member $U$ of which $M|_U\cong R|_U^{\oplus r_U}$ for a finite integer $r_U\geq0$, using slice restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then $M$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and the complex $M[0]$ concentrated in degree zero is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For every morphism $\varphi:R\to B$ of sheaves of commutative rings on the same site, the canonical comparison is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$:
$$B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}(B\otimes_R M)[0].$$
Use derived extension of scalars as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and ordinary scalar extension as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The $B$-module sheaf $B\otimes_R M$ is locally finite free with the same local ranks, and the comparison is natural in $M$. No flatness of $B$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GN1, lemma-flatness-sheafification-refined: local flatness; the degree-zero derived scalar comparison is its K-flat application (proof in report)

proof.text: To prove flatness, take a finite relation $\sum_{p=1}^n a_p s_p=0$ over an object $V$. Choose a covering $\{U_i\to V\}$ trivializing $M$ and let $e_{i1},\ldots,e_{ir_i}$ be the basis sections on $U_i$. The slice restriction formula gives $s_p|_{U_i}=\sum_q b_{ipq}e_{iq}$ with $b_{ipq}\in R(U_i)$. Applying each coordinate of the trivialization to the restricted relation gives $\sum_p a_p|_{U_i}b_{ipq}=0$ for every $q$. These are precisely the finite factorizations required by [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion], with $l_i=r_i$ and $t_{iq}=e_{iq}$; hence $M$ is flat. The empty basis gives the same argument when $r_i=0$.

source.place: Tag 08FC, lemma-flat-eq, condition (2) implies (1), with the factorization given by the local basis; compare Tag 0GN1, lemma-flatness-sheafification-refined

proof.text: The complex $M[0]$ vanishes in degrees greater than zero and its only possibly nonzero term is flat by Step 1. Every zero term is flat because tensoring with zero is the zero exact functor, by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] applies with upper bound zero and shows that $M[0]$ is K-flat.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, applied to a complex concentrated in degree zero

proof.text: For $\varphi:R\to B$, use the identity resolution $M[0]\to M[0]$, now K-flat. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes derived scalar extension by termwise scalar extension on this resolution, giving the canonical isomorphism to $(M\otimes_R B)[0]$. The balancing relations defining the sheaf tensor identify $m\otimes b$ with $b\otimes m$ in the left-factor convention of the statement, compatibly with the $B$-action. This gives the displayed comparison in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$. For a morphism $u:M\to N$ of locally finite free modules, $u[0]$ is a map between their identity K-flat resolutions; both induced maps on the ordinary tensors send $b\otimes m$ to $b\otimes u(m)$. The natural comparison transformation of the left derived functor therefore gives a commuting square. This proves naturality without any flatness assumption on $B$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, for the identity underlying topos and ring map R to B; Tag 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side, and construction before Definition 06YU

proof.text: The statement's operations are those of Step 3. Read [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] in the monoidal abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ with $\otimes_R$ of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], where $R$ is the unit and $B$ a commutative monoid through $\varphi$. Under the unit isomorphism $R\otimes_RM\cong M$ the two maps $B\otimes_RR\otimes_RM\rightrightarrows B\otimes_RM$ both become $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes m$ (balancing), so their coequalizer $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi M$ is $B\otimes_RM$ with $B$ acting on the left factor, which Step 3 identified with the change of rings. The complex $M[0]$ is also K-flat in the sense of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] used by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]: for any complex $P$, the total complexes $P\otimes M[0]$ and $M[0]\otimes P$ are $P^n\otimes_RM$ and $M\otimes_RP^n$ termwise, with differentials $d\otimes1$ up to sign, and $-\otimes_RM$, $M\otimes_R-$ are exact by Step 1 and [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and symmetry; by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] they carry quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Hence the left derived functor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], computed on a K-flat resolution, may be computed on the identity resolution of $M[0]$, giving $(B\otimes_RM)[0]$ with the same canonical comparison map and the same naturality as in Step 3.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), unit and balancing of the sheaf tensor; exactness of flat tensoring per Definition 03ER (definition-flat) applied termwise

proof.text: On each trivializing member $U_i$, [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] identifies $(B\otimes_R M)|_{U_i}$ with $B|_{U_i}\otimes_{R|_{U_i}}M|_{U_i}$. Its pure-tensor formula respects multiplication on the $B$ factor, so this is also $B|_{U_i}$-linear. Under $M|_{U_i}\cong R|_{U_i}^{\oplus r_i}$, the map $b\otimes(a_q)_q\mapsto(b\varphi(a_q))_q$ has inverse $(b_q)_q\mapsto\sum_q b_q\otimes e_{iq}$, by the balancing relations. These formulas commute with restriction and give inverse maps on the sheafified tensors of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Hence $(B\otimes_R M)|_{U_i}\cong B|_{U_i}^{\oplus r_i}$. The same coverings and finite integers $r_i$ prove the required local freeness, including rank zero and the zero ring.
